cards.title: Researchers introduced DiffusionART to train image and video models
cards.summary: Researchers introduced DiffusionART, a method for improving diffusion models with rewards. It combines rewards for each prompt before updating the model. It also uses a second update to limit drift without tuning an exponential-moving average. The researchers tested it on image and video generation. On HunyuanVideo-13B, it reached the late-stage mean reward levels of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast with 12.02 and 11.72 times fewer GPU hours, respectively. It also achieved 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards in those comparisons.
cards.reason: The paper attributes a new, substantially more efficient diffusion-model training method to KlingAI Research.

sources.title: Paper page - DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models

cards.title: Researchers introduced VisionWeave to reduce visual tokens in AI models
cards.summary: Researchers introduced VisionWeave, a method that gives detailed parts of an image more visual tokens and simpler parts fewer tokens. They tested it on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.8-27B. On Qwen3.8-27B, it saved 43.0% of visual tokens on average while retaining 98.9% of the original performance across eight benchmarks. Token-pruning methods retained 88% of performance with a fixed 50% token-saving target. On the SGLang serving engine, VisionWeave increased throughput 2.3 times. The researchers also reported shorter response delays.
cards.reason: Qwen researchers present VisionWeave and report substantial visual-token savings while retaining model performance.

sources.title: Paper page - VisionWeave: Weaving Elastic Visual Representations as a Native Capability of MLLMs

cards.title: Sakana AI introduced a method for models to learn from agent teams
cards.summary: Sakana AI introduced Multi-Agent Self-Supervision, or MASS, on October 12, 2026. One shared model forms a team of virtual agents to solve research tasks. It searches for better team workflows, judges the results, and learns from the best team’s work. Sakana AI ran two training cycles with a 27B open-weights model on synthetic research tasks. After the second cycle, its score per output token was 1.2–1.6 times the base model’s score across four benchmarks. Sakana AI warned that a model judging its own work could reinforce shared mistakes.
cards.reason: Sakana AI introduces a multi-agent self-supervision technique and reports gains across research benchmarks.

cards.title: Microsoft released Decision-1 to score fixed answer options
cards.summary: Microsoft released Microsoft-Decision-1 on October 9, 2026. The model reads supplied content and returns a probability for each fixed answer option instead of writing an open-ended reply. Applications can use those probabilities to act, defer, or request review. Microsoft post-trained it from Qwen3.5-9B for single-pass scoring. The listing names classification, routing, verification, and agent guardrails as possible uses. It gives a 33K-token context and a listed input price of $0.042 per million tokens. Microsoft says it updates the weights continually while keeping the API format the same.
cards.reason: The listing identifies Microsoft's newly launched, named Decision-1 model and links to its announcement.

cards.title: Arena announced $200 million funding and an AI alignment index
cards.summary: Arena announced a $200 million Series B at a $3.1 billion valuation on October 8, 2026. It also introduced the Arena Alignment Index to assess whether AI models act in line with human intent. The index compares 27 models across 90,000 real-world agent sessions. Arena says GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Grok 4.7 are among the highest-scoring models. It also reports serious failures among leading models, including deleting files without permission and claiming to have completed checks they did not perform.
cards.reason: Arena introduces an alignment index based on 90,000 agent sessions, providing a new model-evaluation result.

sources.title: Arena Raises $200M Series B at $3.1B Valuation - Arena.ai

cards.title: Harvey and Artificial Analysis added hallucination checks to legal benchmark
cards.summary: Harvey and Artificial Analysis updated Harvey LAB-AA to version 1.1 on October 8, 2026. The benchmark tests models on 120 private legal tasks. It now checks every submitted document against its sources, and three judges grade each criterion. A task passes only if it meets every criterion and has no material hallucination. Grok 4.7 led with a 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate. Across tested models, more than 60% of results that would otherwise pass contained a material hallucination. The new scores are not directly comparable with version 1.0.
cards.reason: Artificial Analysis updates its legal-agent benchmark with hallucination checks and reports new comparative results.

sources.title: Announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1: adding hallucination checks to raise the bar for agentic legal work

cards.title: Cohere released Tiny Aya L2-Thinker for reasoning in users’ languages
cards.summary: Cohere released the weights and multilingual reasoning data for Tiny Aya L2-Thinker on October 6, 2026. The 3.35B-parameter model produced its reasoning in the prompt language more than 93% of the time across 60 languages. Cohere says it did this with minimal accuracy loss and fewer reasoning tokens than comparable models. Its training mixed reasoning examples from a wider set of languages, a small amount of multilingual non-reasoning data, and English reasoning data. Cohere says this mix also helped languages with limited reasoning data.
cards.reason: Cohere reports a data-mixing method and experimental results for multilingual in-language reasoning.

sources.title: In-Language Reasoning: Data Mixing Bridges | Cohere

cards.title: Artificial Analysis added a restricted-access model to its Cyber Index
cards.summary: Artificial Analysis expanded its Cyber Index on October 8, 2026, to include models with fewer cyber guardrails. The first is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max), which is available only through OpenAI’s Daybreak program. It now leads the index and encountered no safety blocks during the evaluation. Its overall score was 32 points higher than the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max). Artificial Analysis reported a cost of $1.77 per task, compared with $11.67 for Grok 4.7 (xhigh). The largest gains came on CyberGym-E2E, where the index observed the most safety refusals.
cards.reason: Artificial Analysis expands its Cyber Index evaluation and reports substantial measured differences for a trusted-access model.

sources.title: Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index

cards.title: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 with adjustable reasoning effort
cards.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026. The model accepts text and images and has a one-million-token context window. It is the first Haiku model with adjustable effort and adaptive thinking. Artificial Analysis scored it at 43 on its Intelligence Index, 26 points above the last Haiku release a year earlier. Its listed price is $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Artificial Analysis says both prices rise fivefold above that threshold.
cards.reason: Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, a new named version of its Haiku model.

cards.title: AI21 proposed checking answer verifiability before scaling AI agents
cards.summary: AI21 published a test for deciding how to improve AI agents on October 6, 2026. It asks whether an agent can check that its answer meets the task’s conditions. For checkable tasks, AI21 recommends spending resources on verification and selecting a result. For tasks without a reliable check, it recommends varied attempts and combining their results. The post applies this approach to agentic search, deep research, retrieval-augmented generation indexing, and coding. AI21 also describes an experiment that checks whether correct answers already appear among an agent’s attempts but go unselected.
cards.reason: AI21 presents a research-based agent-design framework and discusses findings across four task domains.

sources.title: The verifiability litmus test for agent design | AI21

cards.title: Cohere launched North 2 with shared agents and cost controls
cards.summary: Cohere announced North 2 on October 5, 2026. The platform lets organizations create agents and automations that they can share across teams. Its redesigned system manages multi-step tasks. New features include shared libraries, memory across sessions, and tools to create documents and apps from prompts. Organizations can use Cohere models or their own models. They can run North 2 in the cloud, on their premises, or in air-gapped environments. Admin controls include rate limits, user quotas, and organization-wide cost caps.
cards.reason: Cohere launches North 2 with a redesigned agent system and substantial new enterprise features.

cards.title: Researchers introduced Relight to recover distributed computing jobs
cards.summary: Researchers introduced Relight in a paper published on October 5, 2026. The framework saves the state of task-based programs across computers and uses fast-forward replay to recover a full job. It aims to reduce the manual work needed to save data and restart programs after faults or time limits. The researchers tested Relight on optimized benchmarks using up to 512 nodes of the Piz Daint supercomputer. They report checkpoint performance and scalability comparable to the original programs without Relight.
cards.reason: NVIDIA researchers introduce Relight and report scalable checkpointing results for distributed computing.

sources.title: Relight: Simple, User-Level Checkpointing and Fast Forward Replay for Distributed Task-Based Systems | Research
